commits.pr_title: [CI][Docs] Fix decode/prefill consistency test prefix construction; add GLM-4-9B and Phi-4 to batch-invariant tested models
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Two related changes, both following the review on this PR:

1. **Fix a soundness bug in `tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py::test_decode_logprobs_match_prefill_logprobs`.** The test rebuilt each prefill prefix from *text* and re-encoded it; `encode(decode(ids))` is not lossless for BPE tokenizers, so the "prefill" could evaluate a different token sequence than decode did and report false mismatches. The prefix is now built directly from token ids (`prompt_token_ids + decode_token_ids[:i]`), which also removes an O(N²) extra `llm.generate` per decoded token. This is the fix from #43317 (@Evangade), carried here at the maintainer's request after that PR went stale; the standalone tokenizer regression test from #43317 is dropped per the review there. Original report by @xRay2016 in #27433.
2. **Add `zai-org/glm-4-9b-chat` and `microsoft/phi-4` to the tested-model list**, following the [invitation to submit model validations without a separate issue](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53247#issuecomment-5374419058).

Why the fix matters here: GLM was originally removed from this PR because the official suite reported a decode/prefill mismatch. Root cause (see the comments below): the model emits `'.'` + `'Here'` as `[13, 8419]`, which re-encodes to the single token `89329` (`'.Here'`), so the text-based prefix diverged from position 11 onward. With token-id prefixes GLM is fully green. Any model whose greedy output hits a BPE merge point can false-fail the unfixed test the same way.

Not a duplicate: #43317 proposes the same test fix but has had no author activity since the May review and is marked stale; this PR carries that commit with its original authorship and sign-off instead of opening another PR.

## Test Plan

Official suite, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, vLLM 0.28.0 (cu129 wheel), torch 2.13.0, Triton 3.7.1, RTX 4090 D (sm89) and H20 (sm90):

```bash
VLLM_TEST_MODEL=<model> pytest tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py -v
```

Plus a controlled A/B of the prefix construction on GLM (same engine instance, 4 prompts × 16 positions, FLASH_ATTN, compiled) and the fixed test re-run on GLM and on the default model.

## Test Result

| Model | RTX 4090 D (sm89), v0.28.0 | H20 (sm90), v0.28.0 | H100 NVL (sm90), nightly 0.28.1rc1.dev580 — run by @yuvalluria ([Phi-4](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53692#issuecomment-5618510438), [GLM](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53692#issuecomment-5619365843)) | RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (sm120), v0.29.0 cu130 wheel, driver 580.159 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B` (suite default), fixed test | 1 passed; full file 19 passed | — | — | full file **19/19 passed** (17:58) |
| `microsoft/phi-4` | not run (24 GB) | 19/19 passed | 19/19 passed (fixed test file) | **19/19 passed** (25:45) |
| `zai-org/glm-4-9b-chat` (unfixed test) | 12/19 — 6 needle cells OOM on 24 GB at init, 1 = the decode/prefill false mismatch | 18/19 — the decode/prefill false mismatch | — | — |
| `zai-org/glm-4-9b-chat`, prefix A/B (unfixed vs token-id) | text re-encode: 59/64; token ids: **64/64 bitwise** | — | — | — |
| `zai-org/glm-4-9b-chat`, fixed test | 1 passed (was FAILED before the fix) | — | **19/19 passed**, incl. `test_decode_logprobs_match_prefill_logprobs[FLASH_ATTN]` | full file **19/19 passed** (24:38), incl. `test_decode_logprobs_match_prefill_logprobs[FLASH_ATTN]` |

sm120 notes: all three backends the suite parametrizes (FLASH_ATTN, TRITON_ATTN, FLEX_ATTENTION) start and pass under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` on this GPU; no reruns were needed (0 flaky retries). This is, as far as the tracker shows, the first run of the determinism suite on an sm120 part.

AI assistance was used for implementation (Claude, Codex); every changed line was reviewed and every command above was run by the human submitter, except the H100 NVL column, which was run and posted by @yuvalluria.

commits.pr_title: [Misc][Platform] Check aligned KV block sizes against every attention backend
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Follow-up to #49845. Phase 1 there picks a KV cache block size every attention
backend accepts. The hybrid and heterogeneous-KV alignment steps that run
afterwards still round by the first backend's kernel block only, as
@Sanjays2402 pointed out in review of #49845, so they can land on a size a
sibling backend rejects. Today that surfaces late, as the opaque
`select_common_block_size()` error at worker setup.

This PR does not change how alignment rounds. It validates the result: if
alignment changed the block size, every backend's `supports_block_size()` must
accept it, otherwise it raises immediately and names the rejecting backends. I
don't know of a model configuration that hits this today, so this is hardening
rather than a fix for an observed failure.

## Why not round by every backend

An earlier revision rounded by the LCM of each backend's smallest kernel block.
That regresses valid configurations: with a backend supporting `[32, 48]` and an
exact-size `[48]` backend, phase 1 correctly picks 48, and the LCM rounding
bumps it to 96, which the exact-size backend rejects. Choosing an aligned size
every backend accepts would need a candidate search inside the mamba and indexer
alignment logic, which is a larger change. Thanks @yewentao256 and
@jayzuccarelli for working through this.

The check is per backend rather than a common-size check across all backends.
Kernel sizes are chosen per KV cache group at runtime, so a global check can
reject configurations that work, and it would bypass backends' exact-size
overrides of `supports_block_size()`.

## Changes

- `update_block_size_for_backend()` records the block size before alignment and
  calls a new `_check_aligned_block_size()` afterwards.
- `CpuPlatform.update_block_size_for_backend()` overrides the base method and
  aligns directly, so it calls the same check.
- `XPUPlatform.update_block_size_for_backend()` rounds the block size up to a
  multiple of 64 for GDN after `super()` has run the check, so it checks that
  rounding too.
- Alignment itself and phase 1 are unchanged.

## Test Plan

Added to `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py`:

- `test_alignment_rejected_by_a_sibling_backend_raises`, run for both the base
  and CPU platforms: an alignment that lands on 32 beside an exact-size `[16]`
  backend raises, naming that backend.
- `test_xpu_gdn_rounding_rejected_by_a_sibling_backend_raises`: XPU's GDN
  rounding from 16 to 64 beside an exact-size `[16]` backend raises. It skips
  without `vllm_xpu_kernels`, like the existing XPU tests.

## Test Result

Ran the three tests locally in a CPU environment with the XPU kernel modules
stubbed: all pass, and the XPU test fails with the XPU check removed. Full
pre-commit is clean.

commits.pr_title: [CI] Stop requiring both API servers to record weight sync metrics
commits.pr_body:
The test asserted that both API servers recorded a weight operation. 

The API servers share one listening socket, so the kernel can send every connection to one server. It was sending all 64 syncs allowed by #59507 to one server and still failed. 

Adding up metrics across processes is already covered by test_in_flight_is_summed_across_api_server_processes, so this drops the check and keeps the count and in-flight checks with a fixed 8 syncs. 

Verified locally on MI300X: 6/6 passes, including a run where only one API server handled requests

## Purpose

`ROCM_ATTN` stores the decoder window as `(W - 1, 0)`, where `W - 1` is the left span. The underlying [decode](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/4c2d277643e217344056e1d2c42115d5f005912f/vllm/v1/attention/ops/chunked_prefill_paged_decode.py#L234) and [prefix-prefill](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/4c2d277643e217344056e1d2c42115d5f005912f/vllm/v1/attention/ops/prefix_prefill.py#L435) kernels use `query_position - key_position < SLIDING_WINDOW`, so their argument must be the total window length `W`, including the current token. Passing `W - 1` excludes the oldest valid token; for `W=1`, passing zero disables the window entirely.

This PR passes `1 + self.sliding_window[0]` to `chunked_prefill_paged_decode`. This matches the existing [KV-cache docstring example](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/4c2d277643e217344056e1d2c42115d5f005912f/vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py#L1160): with `sliding_window=4` and seven computed tokens, the next token at position 7 must attend to tokens **4–7**. The old argument is 3 and attends to **5–7**; the corrected argument is 4 and attends to **4–7**.

`TRITON_ATTN` [stores the same `(W - 1, 0)` tuple](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/4c2d277643e217344056e1d2c42115d5f005912f/vllm/v1/attention/backends/triton_attn.py#L511) and already passes [`SLIDING_WINDOW=(1 + window_size[0])`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/4c2d277643e217344056e1d2c42115d5f005912f/vllm/v1/attention/ops/triton_unified_attention.py#L1133). Applying the same conversion makes the causal window boundaries consistent between the two backends. The no-window sentinel maps to zero, which the helper treats as disabled; encoder attention uses a separate path.

Open-PR searches on 2026-10-01 found no duplicate. Related #49588, #53628, and #59132 do not modify this backend argument conversion.

## Test Plan

Run the focused backend regression and the existing cached-KV boundary test:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_prefix_prefill.py \
  -k 'rocm_backend_sliding_window or cached_kv_block_table_boundary' -q
```

## Test Result

Before the fix, all four windowed regression cases fail and both no-window controls pass. After the fix: **7 passed**, including the existing boundary test. All applicable pre-commit checks passed.

Gemma3 1B IT (BF16, window 512) completed inference on Radeon 890M (`gfx1150`) with inputs within and beyond the window, including chunked prefill and HIP graph decode. Compared before/after ROCM_ATTN with TRITON_ATTN and Transformers FP32. Before/after prompt logprobs were identical for input lengths up to 512; longer inputs showed changes, with errors against the reference implementations increasing or decreasing depending on input length.

AI assistance was used during implementation, testing, and preparation of this PR. vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill was used to review the change.

### Purpose

Add automatic `pooling` labels so pooling reviewers can find relevant PRs and issues.

### AI assistance disclosure

Codex (GPT-6) drafted the code change and ran local validation.

commits.pr_title: [CI] Bump peft to satisfy transformers 5.18 minimum
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

#59621 bumped the pinned transformers to 5.18.0, which raised `MIN_PEFT_VERSION` from 0.19.1 to 0.20.0, but left `peft==0.19.1` pinned in the test lockfiles. The granite-speech HF reference path now fails with:

```
ValueError: The version of PEFT you are using is not compatible, please use a version >= 0.20.0
```

## Claims

- Raises the `peft` floor in `requirements/test/{cuda,rocm}.in` to `>=0.20.0`.
- Regenerates `requirements/test/{cuda,rocm,cpu}.txt`; the only change in each is `peft==0.19.1` -> `peft==0.21.1`.

## Validation

Lockfiles regenerated with the repo's pre-commit hooks:

```bash
pre-commit run pip-compile --files requirements/test/cuda.in
pre-commit run pip-compile-rocm --files requirements/test/rocm.in
pre-commit run pip-compile-cpu --files requirements/test/cuda.in
```

The granite-speech and phi-4-mm tests have not been run locally; relying on CI for those.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][XPU] Make DeepSeek V4 FP8 sparse decode graph-capturable
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fix DeepSeek-V4-Flash failing to start on XPU with graph capture enabled:

```
RuntimeError: Worker failed with error 'level_zero backend failed with error: 44 (UR_RESULT_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE)'
```

**Root cause:** `xpu_sparse_decode_fp8` used `.item()` host syncs, data-dependent tensor shapes, and a per-token Python loop. Level Zero graph capture doesn't support any of these.

**Changes:** Rewrite `xpu_sparse_decode_fp8` to use static shapes and vectorized index construction without host syncs, making it graph-capture safe to fix this bug.


## Test Plan

Start a DeepSeek-V4-Flash server on XPU with graph capture. The test cmds are as follows:

```
# EP4xDP2
ACC_LIMIT=256 VLLM_ALLOW_LONG_MAX_MODEL_LEN=1  VLLM_XPU_ENABLE_XPU_GRAPH=1 \
VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 DISABLE_EAGER=True   python3 -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \
--model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash --port 8123 --host localhost --trust-remote-code --gpu-memory-util=0.85 \
--max-model-len=8192   --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-num-seqs 2 --enable-expert-parallel  --data-parallel-size 2     -tp=4  
# TP4xPP2
ACC_LIMIT=256 VLLM_ALLOW_LONG_MAX_MODEL_LEN=1  VLLM_XPU_ENABLE_XPU_GRAPH=1 \
VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 DISABLE_EAGER=True   python3 -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \
--model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash --port 8123 --host localhost --trust-remote-code --gpu-memory-util=0.85 \
--max-model-len=8192   --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-num-seqs 2 -pp 2     -tp=4
# TP8
ACC_LIMIT=256 VLLM_ALLOW_LONG_MAX_MODEL_LEN=1  VLLM_XPU_ENABLE_XPU_GRAPH=1 \
VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 DISABLE_EAGER=True   python3 -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \
--model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash --port 8123 --host localhost --trust-remote-code --gpu-memory-util=0.85 \
--max-model-len=8192   --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-num-seqs 2     -tp=8
```

## Test Result

- **Before:** server fails to start with the errors above.
- **After:** server starts normally and serves requests, the server hits another startup failure under pipeline parallelism:

```
RuntimeError: Worker failed with error '', please check the stack trace above for the root cause
```

## Purpose

Mono audio with an explicit channel dimension can fail in Whisper preprocessing.
For example, passing a `(1, 16000)` waveform at 16 kHz through the offline audio
tuple path raises `ValueError: Failed to apply WhisperProcessor`, while the same
samples in a `(16000,)` array work.

`normalize_audio` returns early when the input channel count already matches
the target, leaving a 2D array for mono input. This also makes
`AudioProcessorItems.get_audio_length()` report 1 instead of 16000.

Return the only channel as a 1D waveform when the target is mono. Extend the
existing NumPy, Torch and parser tests to cover both channel layouts and the
single-sample case.

This reproduces without resampling. #47693 changes the order of normalization
and resampling, #56023 addresses unsupported multi-channel reduction, and
#51022 optimizes downmixing. Their current patches leave this early return
unchanged.

## Test Plan

Run the audio and parser tests on CPU:

```bash
export VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1
export PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 PYTHONPATH=.

.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/multimodal/test_audio.py \
  -k 'mono_passthrough_for_numpy or mono_passthrough_for_torch or parser_mono_passthrough' -q

.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/multimodal/test_audio.py tests/multimodal/test_parse.py \
  -k 'not torchaudio and not resampling_with_channel_normalization_e2e' -q

SKIP=actionlint .venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/multimodal/audio.py tests/multimodal/test_audio.py
```

Also compare the same one-second WAV in `(16000,)`, `(1, 16000)` and `(16000, 1)`
layouts through vLLM's Whisper multimodal processor, using the official
`openai/whisper-tiny` configuration, tokenizer and feature extractor.

## Test Result

- Focused regression cases: **8 failed, 3 passed before; 11 passed after**.
- Audio and parser selection on main `fa1b3b1922` plus this patch:
  **71 passed, 1 skipped, 8 deselected**.
- Whisper preprocessing: both 2D layouts failed before. After the fix, all
  three layouts produce exactly equal features, prompt tokens and placeholder
  ranges. Feature shape is `(1, 80, 3000)` and parsed audio length is 16000.
- Applicable pre-commit hooks passed. Actionlint was skipped; no workflows changed.

The local environment has no matching torchaudio build. An earlier full audio
test run had 55 passes and 7 failures due to that missing dependency; the
filtered run excludes those cases and the default-backend assertion. The
skipped parser test requires CUDA. Whisper validation covers CPU preprocessing;
model generation and accuracy evaluation have not been run.

AI assistance was used, and I reviewed all the changes and tests.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Release pending CPU lookup pins on cache reset
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Release SimpleCPUOffload lookup-only CPU block references during cache reset. A request waiting for GPU allocation can otherwise prevent `reset_prefix_cache(reset_connector=True)` from succeeding even after GPU blocks and in-flight transfers have drained.

## Claims

- Reset releases temporary CPU lookup pins and invalidates their saved lookup state.
- Existing in-flight DMA references remain protected until completion.
- A deterministic regression covers eager/lazy modes and one/two cache groups.

## Validation

Validated against upstream `5f30fc7031cae49bf51073fc953d419b08f8887c`, using its matching precompiled native extensions.

| Check | Unpatched + regression | Patched |
|---|---|---|
| New reset regression | 4 assertion failures (`reset()` returns False) | 4 pass within the full scheduler suite |
| Scheduler, KV events, connector and metrics suites | — | 92 passed |
| CUDA worker suite, RTX 4090 | — | 21 passed |
| Real Scheduler allocation-pressure diagnostic | Reset fails after GPU blocks are released | Reset succeeds; retry has no stale CPU hit |
| Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct GPU diagnostic | 16 lookup references prevent reset | References released; reset and subsequent generation pass |

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py -k test_reset_releases_pending_cpu_hits
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_kv_events.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_simple_cpu_offload_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_simple_cpu_offload_metrics.py
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_worker.py
pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/manager.py tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/manager.py tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py
```

All applicable changed-file hooks, mypy 3.10/3.12 and `git diff --check` passed. The existing Buildkite KV Offload suite collects the new test; test tethering passed. Upstream CI has not run for this candidate.

The GPU diagnostic used MRV2, FP16, TP=1, eager execution and 128 MiB each of GPU/CPU KV cache. After a real CPU store/load round trip with 256 cached tokens, it explicitly paused a queued request after the production CPU lookup. Baseline reset returned False; the patch released all 16 lookup pins, reset successfully and generated the same token `[19]` with zero cached tokens. Actual allocation pressure is covered separately by the real Scheduler diagnostic, whose worker token output is synthetic. This is a focused correctness check, not a performance or broad model-quality claim. Multi-node, disk/GDS and other GPU backends were not validated.

## Details

`get_num_new_matched_tokens()` pins matching CPU blocks until `update_state_after_alloc()` consumes the lookup. Failed GPU allocation leaves that lookup in `_pending_cpu_hits`. Reset already abandons transfers safely but omitted these pre-allocation references.

Reuse `_free_pending_cpu_hit()` before clearing the pending lookup map. These references have no associated worker DMA; submitted transfers retain their separate pins and existing completion-based cleanup. A waiting request performs a fresh lookup when scheduling resumes. No API, storage format or normal scheduling policy changes are introduced.

Duplicate screening on 2026-10-03 covered open/closed/merged PRs, related issues, recent commits and the contributor's existing PRs. [#42289](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/42289) introduced temporary lookup pins; [#39726](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/39726) introduced reset support. Both are merged. The active [#57816](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57816) addresses eager-store placement after MRV2 preemption, a different state transition. No active implementation of this lookup-pin reset fix was found. This draft does not claim to close an existing issue.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex performed investigation, implementation, local/remote validation and drafting. The human contributor has confirmed review of the final change and authorized submission. The reported validation was performed with Codex; independent human reruns have not been confirmed.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Responses API] Reuse streamed item ids in final harmony response
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes the harmony (gpt-oss) part of #59834; #59307 fixed the non-harmony path. When `/v1/responses` streams, `response.completed` rebuilds its output from the harmony messages with `harmony_to_response_output`. That rebuild mints a new item `id` and function `call_id`, which no longer match the ones sent in `response.output_item.added`/`done`, so strict clients abort.

- `_process_harmony_streaming_events` records, for each completed harmony message, the items sent in its `output_item.done` events (`HarmonyContext.streamed_items_by_message`).
- `responses_full_generator` matches each message to its own record by object identity. `reuse_streamed_item_ids` then copies `id`/`call_id` onto that message's rebuilt items by type. Content and `incomplete` status still come from the rebuild. Items that were never streamed (zero-delta) keep a new id.
- Streamed harmony reasoning items now use the `rs_` prefix instead of `msg_`, matching the non-streaming path and the non-harmony path.

Matching per message matters. A built-in `python` call streams as `code_interpreter_call` but is rebuilt as `reasoning`. If ids were matched across messages, that call would take the streamed id of the next reasoning item.

## Testing

`vllm serve openai/gpt-oss-20b --no-enable-prefix-caching` (1x H200), then the request from the issue:

```bash
curl -sN localhost:8000/v1/responses -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "model": "openai/gpt-oss-20b", "stream": true,
  "input": "Call the get_weather tool for Paris. You must call the tool now.",
  "tools": [{"type": "function", "name": "get_weather", "parameters": {"type": "object",
    "properties": {"city": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["city"]}}]
}' | sed -n 's/^data: //p' | jq -c '
  if .type == "response.output_item.done" then ["done", .item.type, .item.id, .item.call_id]
  elif .type == "response.completed" then .response.output[] | ["completed", .type, .id, .call_id]
  else empty end'
```

main (5f30fc7): `completed` changes every id.
```
["done","reasoning","msg_832f7cd8a3888df4",null]
["done","function_call","fc_8019379c1a695c28","call_b07a9991be290d4c"]
["completed","reasoning","rs_b5c9be54d08ca702",null]
["completed","function_call","fc_bc041d3276faf22e","call_bc041d3276faf22e"]
```
This PR: `completed` keeps the streamed ids.
```
["done","reasoning","rs_a972e97aaf1f0eb1",null]
["done","function_call","fc_be95d8cf99657077","call_84160cffacc40ff2"]
["completed","reasoning","rs_a972e97aaf1f0eb1",null]
["completed","function_call","fc_be95d8cf99657077","call_84160cffacc40ff2"]
```

I ran the same check, 3 times each, on a forced tool call, a reasoning + text answer, and a `max_output_tokens=40` cut-off (`incomplete`). Results: main had id mismatches in 9/9 runs, and this PR in 0/9.

Other tests:
- `tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_serving_responses.py`: 64 passed. The 2 new tests fail on main.
- `tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_harmony.py` (gpt-oss-20b e2e): 37 passed, 2 skipped, 1 xpassed on both main and this PR.

No change to generated content: only item ids change, so no eval is needed.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Preserve abort finish_reason for scale-out token streams
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

In token mode, `/inference/v1/generate` streams skip engine outputs that have no new token IDs. An abort always ends with such an output (`token_ids=[]`, `finish_reason="abort"`), so an aborted stream ends with `[DONE]` and no `finish_reason`. The only exception is when the abort happens to be merged into a pending token delta. Text mode (#58588) and the Rust frontend already emit every terminal output.

- Every output that has a `finish_reason` is now emitted, in both output modes.
- The per-choice token counter is now sized by `sampling_params.n`. It was sized from the first output, which with `n > 1` may hold only choice 0. The next choice then raised `IndexError`, and the stream ended in a 500 error chunk.

## Test Plan

Live server on H200 with `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`. The same requests went to `main` (bc21cba967) and to this PR:

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --max-model-len 2048 --no-enable-prefix-caching --tokens-only
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --max-model-len 2048 --no-enable-prefix-caching --enable-scale-out --max-num-seqs 1
```

Each request was a streamed `/inference/v1/generate` call with `max_tokens: 900`, `ignore_eos: true` and `include_usage`. It was aborted through `/abort_requests` (or `/inference/v1/abort_requests`) once the first token chunk arrived. With `--max-num-seqs 1`, a second request could also be aborted while still queued.

## Test Result

| Case | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| tokens mode, abort mid-stream (also with `logprobs` / `flat_logprobs`) | no `finish_reason` unless the abort merged into a token chunk | final chunk `token_ids: [], finish_reason: "abort"` (`logprobs: {"content": []}`) |
| abort while queued (0 tokens) | no choice chunk | one `abort` chunk |
| `n=2`, abort mid-stream | `list index out of range` 500 chunk in 4/7 runs | both choices get `abort`, 12/12 runs |
| text-mode abort, non-stream abort, `length` / EOS `stop` | — | unchanged |

Usage `completion_tokens` matched the streamed token count in every case.

## Summary

- Select TRTLLM for node-local all-reduce groups under automatic backend selection.
- Only attempt MNNVL automatically for multi-node Blackwell groups.
- Disable automatic FlashInfer all-reduce fusion for multi-node Hopper groups, where neither backend is supported.
- Validate TRTLLM eligibility against the all-reduce group rather than the global distributed environment.

## Testing

- `python3 -m compileall -q vllm/distributed/device_communicators/flashinfer_all_reduce.py`
- Targeted pytest collection was attempted, but this environment lacks the existing `ray` test dependency (`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'ray'`).

commits.pr_title: [Feature] Release the CUDA graph pool on sleep
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

With sleep mode on, CUDA graphs keep their private tensor pools resident after `sleep()` has unmapped weights and KV cache. On large MoE deployments this is GiBs per GPU that sleep cannot release. This PR adds an opt-in, `sleep_mode_offload_cudagraph` (off by default), that captures CUDA graphs into a dedicated cuMem-backed pool, so sleep releases their physical memory and wake remaps the same virtual addresses. Graphs are not recaptured. With the option off, behaviour is identical to main: plain graph pools, custom allreduce registers graph buffers, `NCCL_GRAPH_REGISTER` is untouched.

The design follows SGLang's `SGLANG_MEMORY_SAVER_CUDA_GRAPH` (off by default; sgl-project/sglang#7873, #32718, #40648); the table below compares the two item by item.

It is based on the graph-pool design from aoshen02/vllm#50 (same author), ported to current main, plus two fixes needed on multi-GPU deployments.

**Based on main, which now includes #59156 and #59158 (both merged)**: per-tag pool lists in `CuMemAllocator.allocator_and_pools`, and the rule that any wake restores every tag other than `weights` and `kv_cache`. With #59158's `runtime` tag, `CuMemBackend.suspend()` offloads `("weights", "runtime", "cudagraph")` at level 1 and `("runtime", "cudagraph")` at level 2.

**Must merge after #59228** (free-while-asleep fix in `csrc/cumem_allocator.cpp`). Without it, tearing down a cuMem graph pool while asleep (for example deleting the engine during sleep) double-unmaps it and leaves a sticky CUDA error. The weights and KV pools already have this failure on main; this PR extends it to the graph pool.

### Enabling it

```python
llm = LLM(model, enable_sleep_mode=True, sleep_mode_offload_cudagraph=True)
```

```bash
vllm serve <model> --enable-sleep-mode --sleep-mode-offload-cudagraph
```

`sleep_mode_offload_cudagraph` is a `ModelConfig` field next to `enable_sleep_mode` and `sleep_mode_backend` (the name keeps their `sleep_mode_` prefix and says what it does to graphs). It reaches `ModelConfig` through `EngineArgs` like its neighbours, with the CLI flag `--sleep-mode-offload-cudagraph` next to `--enable-sleep-mode`.

The pool is active when the option is on, `enable_sleep_mode` is on, the sleep backend is `cumem`, CUDA graphs are on and the platform is CUDA (`VllmConfig.use_cumem_cudagraph_pool`, the single predicate that the capture routing, `CudaCommunicator` and the NCCL default all read). If the option is on but another requirement is not met, the pool is simply not used and startup logs one warning saying which requirement is missing.

**Benefit when on:** graph memory is released while asleep at both levels (DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP4 + EP: 2.3 GiB/GPU; DeepSeek-V4.1 TP8: 7.43 GiB/GPU; Qwen3-8B TP1: 332 MiB). **Cost when on:** pinned host memory for the pool's backup, also at level 2; about +3 % decode TPOT at concurrency 1 from the custom-allreduce copy (within noise at concurrency 16 and above); 0.05–0.1 s more per sleep.

### SGLang parity

| Item | SGLang | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Switch | env `SGLANG_MEMORY_SAVER_CUDA_GRAPH`, default off | config field `sleep_mode_offload_cudagraph`, default off |
| Preconditions unmet | pool not used, silently | pool not used; one startup warning naming the missing requirement |
| Graph pool across sleep | backed up and restored (#32718, #40804) | backed up at both levels, restored by any wake |
| `NCCL_GRAPH_REGISTER` | defaulted to `0` when active (#40648) | `setdefault("0")` when active; an explicit value wins with a warning |
| Custom allreduce | unregistered capture (#7873), keyed on the env alone | unregistered only when the pool is active (same predicate) |
| Runners | single runner | Model Runner V2 capture sites; on V1 see the limitation below |
| Recapture | n/a | elastic EP releases the pool before recapture |

### Scope

- Runner-agnostic predicate; the capture sites and tests are those of Model Runner V2, and V1 code is unchanged. Covered capture paths all go through one helper, `use_cudagraph_pool()` in `vllm/compilation/cudagraph_pool.py` (next to the capture sites, which keeps the NCCL `set_graph_pool_id` coupling at the compilation layer). It gets the allocator through `get_mem_allocator_instance()`; the predicate already requires CUDA, so that is `CuMemAllocator` (a narrow cast at the call site rather than new `MemAllocator` protocol methods, which XPU's allocator would not implement):
  - V2 FULL graphs (`CudaGraphManager.capture`, including DBO microbatch capture on the ubatch capture stream);
  - compiled PIECEWISE graphs (`CUDAGraphWrapper`);
  - breakable CUDA graph segments (`BreakableCUDAGraphWrapper`);
  - speculator graphs (autoregressive/EAGLE/MTP, DFlash, DSpark), which subclass `CudaGraphManager` and reuse its `capture()`.
- Memory profiling is deliberately *not* routed through cuMem: V2's `profile_cudagraph_memory()` captures inside `plain_cudagraph_capture()` (a `ContextVar`), so destroying the profiling graphs frees their pool as before.
- **V1 limitation:** with the option on under Model Runner V1, V1's profiling graphs stay in the cuMem pool (awake +326 MiB on Qwen3-8B, +1.6 GiB on DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP4, not counted in the KV-cache estimate) and V1 DBO microbatch graphs stay in the plain pool; outputs are unaffected.
- Out of scope: encoder CUDA graphs (the encoder runner keeps its own `graph_pool_handle()`), and the Gemma4 centroids graphs in the V1 spec-decode path.

### Design

- **One graph pool, tagged `cudagraph`.** All routed captures share the process's single graph pool, as they share the global graph pool without sleep mode. `CuMemAllocator.use_cudagraph_pool()` creates one pluggable-allocator `MemPool` on the first capture, keeps it as a one-entry `cudagraph` list in `allocator_and_pools`, and yields its id for `torch.cuda.graph(pool=...)` while the allocator tags allocations `cudagraph`. There is no `use_mem_pool` (`capture_begin` routes allocations itself) and no trim loop, so reusing the pool is safe. The module-level `use_cudagraph_pool()` also points NCCL's graph allocator (`set_graph_pool_id`) at whichever pool is used, so the capture sites need no separate call.
- **CPU-backed at level 1 and level 2.** A captured pool is not only scratch activations. It can hold values written once at capture time (constants, persistent kernel or attention state) that replay reads but never rewrites. Discarding the pool corrupts those graphs. SGLang hit this and moved to backing up the graph pool across pause/resume (sgl-project/sglang#32718) and to keeping DSA graph state and the pool intact (sgl-project/sglang#40804). The pool is therefore always backed up to host memory, at level 2 as well. This costs pinned host RAM at level 2 as well: the pool is 2.3 GiB/GPU on DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP4 and 7.43 GiB/GPU on DeepSeek-V4.1 TP8 (about 60 GiB per 8-GPU node), in addition to the level-1 weight backup. Discarding the pool was also bit-exact on DeepSeek-V4-Flash (TP2 and TP4, full and selective wakes), but it is not safe in general, so the default stays offload.
- **Sleep policy lives in `CuMemBackend`; the allocator is mechanism only.** `suspend()` offloads `cudagraph` at both levels; like every tag other than `weights` and `kv_cache`, it is restored automatically by any wake, selective or not. The RL flow `wake_up(["weights"])` → update → `wake_up(["kv_cache"])` has graphs replayable once both are awake.
- **Pool lifetime.** The graph `MemPool` is kept together with its pluggable allocator wrapper and released by `release_pools()` like every other pool. Freeing an allocation while asleep (e.g. a graph pool at teardown) needs no spare VRAM and no Python remap: **this PR depends on #59228**, which makes the C++ `my_free` skip unmapping an allocation that `sleep()` already released and only free its address reservation (ROCm already skipped via an empty chunk list).
- **Recapture (elastic EP).** Elastic EP is the only runtime path that drops and recaptures graphs (on every scale). Each capture runs on a new stream (`graph_capture()`), and the caching allocator reuses a freed block of a live pool only on the stream that freed it, so recapturing into the kept pool grew it: DeepSeek-V2-Lite DP2↔4 with sleep mode went from 586 to 5098 MiB of graph pool on rank 0 over five scale cycles. Elastic EP now calls `release_cudagraph_pool()` (a no-op unless the pool is active) right after `release_graphs()` on the V2 path; the V1 path is as on main. Once no graph uses the pool, it is dropped, its segments are unmapped through the free callback, and the next capture starts a fresh pool. It refuses while the pool is asleep (freeing would unmap a second time) or while something still references it, and the message counts the other references and names the possible holders (live graphs, or a capture-time pool reference taken without a release, as NCCL symmetric memory did). That check found that graph release left the PIECEWISE graphs alive in the compiled model's wrappers until the recompile replaced them; `CudaGraphManager.release_graphs()` now clears them too, as profiling teardown already does. No other runtime path releases or recaptures graphs: LoRA and weight updates replay the existing graphs, and profiling captures into a throwaway plain pool.

### Custom allreduce fix

Custom allreduce IPC-registers the buffers that captured graphs read (`register_graph_buffers`). `cudaIpcGetMemHandle` rejects cuMem memory, so capture fails with `csrc/custom_all_reduce.cuh:164 'invalid argument'` and the worker exits. This was reproduced on GB300 with Qwen3-8B TP4, `VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_FLASHINFER=0 VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_SYMM_MEM=0` and `--compilation-config '{"pass_config":{"fuse_allreduce_rms":false}}'`.

When the cuMem graph pool is active, custom allreduce captures with `registered=False`: it copies the input into the pre-registered IPC buffer, which is `cudaMalloc` memory. SGLang does the same (sgl-project/sglang#7873), keyed on its env alone; here it follows the same predicate as the pool. `CudaCommunicator` reads `use_cumem_cudagraph_pool` from the current config once at construction (workers build communicators under `set_current_vllm_config`; without a config there is no sleep-mode policy, so graph buffers stay registered) and passes `register_graph_buffers=False` to `CustomAllreduce`, which itself reads no config and does not look at allocator state during capture. Custom all-gather and reduce-scatter always copy into the pre-registered buffer already, so they need no change. The cost is one device-to-device copy per captured allreduce, the same path eager mode uses, and only when the pool is active. Measured on GB300 (DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP4 + EP, MTP, sleep mode on and awake): over five server restarts per build (four of them with a warmup), median decode TPOT at concurrency 1 is about +3 % for the whole PR (5.35 vs 5.21 ms) and +3.6 % for a control that only forces the copy (no cuMem pool), so the cost is the copy; the cuMem pool itself adds nothing measurable. Main's own restart-to-restart spread is 2.4 %. `NCCL_GRAPH_REGISTER=0` alone costs nothing measurable. At concurrency 16 and above the difference is within run-to-run noise. On MI355X (#59523) the same copy costs +3.4 % (vLLM custom allreduce) and +2.7 % (AITER).

### NCCL graph registration

With `NCCL_GRAPH_REGISTER` enabled, NCCL registers graph-captured user buffers and retains their cuMem handles. That pins about 400–510 MiB/GPU through sleep. After wake remaps new physical memory at the same address, NCCL also keeps stale registrations; in SGLang this caused hangs and wrong results (fzyzcjy/torch_memory_saver#88, sgl-project/sglang#40648). As in #40648, startup (`VllmConfig.__post_init__`, `_verify_cumem_cudagraph_pool`) sets `NCCL_GRAPH_REGISTER=0` when the pool is active and it is unset, before any worker or communicator exists (workers inherit the environment; Ray copies `NCCL_*`). An explicit value is kept, with a warning giving the reason. An earlier revision also refused `TORCH_NCCL_USE_TENSOR_REGISTER_ALLOCATOR_HOOK`. On GB300 (DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP4 + EP and DP4 + EP, hook=1 with that check removed, `NCCL_DEBUG_SUBSYS=REG`), NCCL logged no buffer registration, memory while asleep and after each wake matched hook=0, and outputs matched hook=0, so the check was removed.

### What is not released

Graph executables (`cudaGraphExec_t`) and the driver memory they own are not released. They live outside any PyTorch pool. On DeepSeek-V4-Flash DP4, about 1944 MiB of graph-exec memory plus 1142 MiB charged during capture stay resident per GPU after sleep. Releasing them would require destroying and recapturing graphs, or checkpointing the CUDA process.

### Related work

- #47700 captures CUDA graphs into the `weights` cuMem pool. Graph memory then follows the weights policy: it is discarded at level 2 and restored only with weights. This PR gives graphs their own tag with an always-backup policy, so level-2 sleep and selective wake cannot corrupt captured state. It also covers FULL, compiled PIECEWISE, breakable and speculator capture in both runners.
- #56373 (closed) used CUDA checkpoint of the whole process. That releases everything, including graph executables and the context, but it supports a single GPU only. This PR works with TP/DP and keeps communicators alive, at the cost of the resident graph executables described above.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest -v tests/basic_correctness/memory/cumem/test_cumem.py -k cudagraph_pool
pytest -v tests/basic_correctness/memory/sleep_mode/test_sleep_mode.py -k cudagraph_pool  # TP=2 case needs 2 GPUs
pytest -v tests/v1/worker/test_sleep_mode_backend.py -k cumem_cudagraph_pool
```

- `test_cudagraph_pool_sleep_and_release[sleep-1|sleep-2]` (allocator level): captures are not routed with the policy off or under `plain_cudagraph_capture()`, and are routed with NCCL's graph pool id following the pool. A captured graph that reads a pool-resident constant survives `suspend(level)` → `resume(["kv_cache"])` (which already restores the pool at the same addresses) → `resume(["weights"])` and replays correctly. Release is refused while asleep and while the graph is alive; afterwards the pool is empty and a recapture on a new stream refills it to the same size.
- `test_sleep_cudagraph_pool[...]` (engine level, tiny Llama): for each Model Runner V2 capture site (FULL, PIECEWISE, breakable) graph memory carries the `cudagraph` tag, `NCCL_GRAPH_REGISTER` defaults to `0`, and greedy output is exact after level-1 and level-2 selective wakes; on V2, elastic EP's sequence (`release_graphs()`, `release_cudagraph_pool()`, `capture_model()`) empties the pool and refills it to the same size, twice. The TP=2 case forces the legacy custom allreduce. The `off-by-default` case checks that without the option there is no cuMem graph memory and `NCCL_GRAPH_REGISTER` is untouched.
- `test_cumem_cudagraph_pool_startup_checks[...]`: active pool → `NCCL_GRAPH_REGISTER=0`; an explicit value wins with a warning; not opted in → untouched, no log; opted in but inactive → one warning, env untouched.

## Test Result

**Opt-in and runner-agnostic revision (h200, Qwen3-8B TP1, sleep mode on, this branch on the CI image):**

| Runner | `sleep_mode_offload_cudagraph` | Awake MiB | KV cache tokens | `cudagraph` tag | Asleep MiB | GSM8K awake / after wakes |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| V1 | off | 122379 | 731,296 | 0 | 1741 | 0.8832 / 0.8832 |
| V1 | on | 122705 | 731,296 | 658 MiB | 1411 | 0.8832 / 0.8817 |
| V2 | off | 120437 | 729,808 | 0 | 1555 | 0.8832 / 0.8840 |
| V2 | on | 120437 | 729,808 | 332 MiB | 1223 | 0.8825 / 0.8825 |

- V1 (code as on main): KV cache size is the same with the option on and off, but awake memory is +326 MiB and peak during GSM8K +266 MiB (124913 vs 124647 MiB), because V1's profiling graphs stay in the pool; outputs after full, selective and level-2 wakes are 16/16.
- Probe outputs (16 prompts, greedy) after three rounds of full, selective and level-2 wakes are 14–16/16 in all four arms, the same as three awake repeats without sleep (13–15/16 against the first run), so the differences are run-to-run batching variation, not the option.
- With the option off: no `cudagraph` tag, `NCCL_GRAPH_REGISTER` untouched (engine-level `off-by-default` test).

**Current head (GB300 rack 4, nightly `0cbac6cd1` + #59158 + this PR per file; DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP4 + EP, MTP, V2):**
- GSM8K awake / full wake / selective wake: 0.944 / 0.945 / 0.946 vs 0.947 / 0.951 / 0.941 without this PR (level 2 + reload is broken on V4 either way). Asleep 8945 → 6379 MiB/GPU; `cudagraph` tag 2342 MiB.
- 21-cycle soak (full, weights-first and kv-first selective wakes): memory flat, every probe exact, sleep about 1.0 s and wake 0.6–1.7 s per cycle.
- KV cache size matches the unpatched build to 0.01 %; the profiling graphs are released.
- TP2: exact after full and selective wakes. Qwen3-VL-2B (encoder graphs on) and a Qwen3-0.6B LoRA: exact after every wake order (h200).
- Elastic EP (h200, DeepSeek-V2-Lite, DP2↔4 ×5 with a level-1 sleep/wake after each cycle, Ray backend): the `cudagraph` tag stays at 586 MiB on every scale (it grew to 5098 MiB before the fix). Awake memory on rank 0 after each scale-down is 117341–117355 MiB, versus 117321–117325 MiB for the same build without sleep mode and 118135–118143 MiB on main with sleep mode. The 0.8 GiB below main comes from clearing the previous PIECEWISE graphs in `release_graphs()`, which the build without sleep shows too. Asleep: 6845 MiB vs 8219 MiB on main. Probe outputs match main in every arm (4/4 at DP2; 2/4 at DP4 in every arm, including main, from DP batching nondeterminism).
- Dual batch overlap could not be run on the current GB300 image: Model Runner V2 rejects `--enable-dbo` with speculative decoding, microbatching without MTP needs the DeepEP or NIXL EP all2all backend, and DeepEP low-latency fails at startup on that image (`cudaErrorSymbolNotFound` in `internode_ll.cu`) on main as well. The DBO capture path is covered by code review only.
- Unit tests on h200: `test_cudagraph_pool_policy.py`, `test_cumem.py`, `test_sleep_mode_backend.py`, `test_workspace.py`, the capture-site and TP2 custom-allreduce sleep tests: all pass.

- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: all hooks pass (ruff check/format, mypy, typos, SPDX, forbidden imports, torch.cuda API check, test tethering). `python -m py_compile` passes.
All runs are on GB300 with the nightly image, torch 2.13.0+cu130. The branch also needs the C++ fix from #59228.


**Re-validation after the restructure (head `d5f3bd94fb`, with #59156 underneath), nightly image, GB300.**
- **Unit tests:** `test_cumem.py` + `test_sleep_mode_backend.py`: 26 passed (single GPU). The graph-pool tests also pass with `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True`, so the capture path needs no expandable-segments toggle.
- **DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP4 + EP4 + MTP, gated bit-exact harness** (553 requests per round): asleep **11517 MiB/GPU** with #59156 underneath (this PR alone measured 12839 MiB before the rebase; the difference is #59156 workspace scratch). Every round 553/553 bit-identical to the awake reference after a level-1 full wake and after a level-1 selective wake (weights, then kv_cache). Sleep 1.1-1.2 s, wake 0.6 s.
- **Qwen3-8B with custom allreduce forced** (FlashInfer and symm-mem allreduce off, allreduce+RMSNorm fusion off): TP4 and TP2 both start (the engine died at capture before the custom-allreduce fix), and single-request text and logprobs are identical to before sleep after two sleep/wake cycles; asleep 3497 MiB/GPU at TP4. The TP=2 pytest regression needs hmellor/tiny-random-LlamaForCausalLM, which is not in the offline cache there, so the TP2 check used Qwen3-8B.
- **All sleep PRs merged** (#59156 + #59158 + this PR): asleep **6313 MiB/GPU**, 553/553 bit-identical after full and selective wakes; merged unit tests 29 passed.

- **Unit tests:** `test_cumem.py` 14/14, including both `test_cudagraph_pool_survives_sleep` cases; `test_sleep_mode_backend.py` 9/9.
- **TP=2 custom allreduce regression test:** passed, not skipped. Custom allreduce was active and graph memory carried the `cudagraph` tag.
- **Qwen3-8B TP4 with custom allreduce forced** (FlashInfer/symm-mem allreduce and allreduce+RMSNorm fusion off):
  - Before this change the engine died at capture with `custom_all_reduce.cuh:164 'invalid argument'`. It now starts, and still registers 11972 graph addresses, which are the pre-registered IPC buffer.
  - After a full wake and a selective wake, single-request text and logprobs are identical to before sleep.
- **DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP4 + EP4, MTP, bit-exact:** 553 deterministic requests (batch sizes 1–256) per round.
  - 13 rounds are identical to the awake baseline: 3× full wake, 3× selective wake weights-first, 3× selective wake kv_cache-first, plus awake rounds.
  - Level 2 + `reload_weights` is broken for DeepSeek-V4 on unpatched vLLM as well.
- **Memory while asleep, level 1, per GPU:**

  | Model / setup | Unpatched | This PR | `cudagraph` tag (backed up) |
  |---|---:|---:|---:|
  | DeepSeek-V4-Flash, TP4 + EP4, MTP | 15178 MiB | 12839 MiB (−2339) | 2.29 GiB |
  | GLM-5.3, TP8 over 2 nodes, MTP | 9449 MiB | 8199 MiB (−1250) | 1.22 GiB |
  | DeepSeek-V4.1, TP8 over 2 nodes | 21035 MiB | 13425 MiB (−7610) | 7.43 GiB |

- **Other model families (all sleep PRs combined, TP4):** level-1 full wake, level-1 selective wake and level 2 + `reload_weights` are all bit-exact against the first awake run. The engine used Model Runner V2 on every model.

  | Model | Asleep MiB/GPU, without → with this PR | `cudagraph` tag |
  |---|---:|---:|
  | Qwen3-8B | 3605 → 3561 | 0.04 GiB |
  | Llama-3.1-8B NVFP4 | 3535 → 3491 | 0.04 GiB |

  GSM8K on Qwen3-8B across awake / full wake / selective wake / level 2 + reload: 0.885 / 0.882 / 0.892 / 0.885.
- **Sleep/wake latency:**
  - V4-Flash TP4: first sleep 3.09 s, later sleeps 1.2 s, wake 0.8 s. That is 0.05–0.1 s more than discarding the pool.
  - V4.1: the first level-1 sleep is about 1.7 s slower, because it backs up 7.4 GiB/GPU. Wake time is unchanged.
- **GSM8K on V4.1:** 0.897 / 0.901 / 0.899 for awake / full wake / selective wake, against 0.892 / 0.899 / 0.902 unpatched. Level 2 + reload is broken upstream for DeepSeek-V4.
- **GSM8K on GLM-5.3** (1319 questions, 5-shot, temperature 0):

  | Build | Awake | Level-1 full wake | Level-1 selective wake | Level 2 + `reload_weights` |
  |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
  | Unpatched | 0.914 | 0.914 | 0.918 | 0.911 |
  | This PR | 0.910 | 0.916 | 0.915 | 0.917 |

- **NCCL guards:**
  - `NCCL_GRAPH_REGISTER=1` fails at startup with a clear error (the register-hook check was removed, see "NCCL graph registration").
  - With sleep mode off, `NCCL_GRAPH_REGISTER` is left unset and graph pools stay plain PyTorch pools.
- **Teardown while asleep with the freed VRAM taken by another process** (this PR + #59228): no error, no OOM.

---

AI assistance (Codex, Claude Code) was used for the implementation, porting, review and drafting of this PR. The human submitter is responsible for reviewing the changes and owns them end to end.

### AMD MI355X (ROCm)

This PR is gated on `current_platform.is_cuda()`, so it is inert on ROCm (verified: memory matches #59156 within 6 MiB). Enabling it on ROCm was tried as a local patch, not included here:
- `is_cuda()` → `is_cuda_alike()` alone fails at the first capture: a blocking `hipMemset` in `csrc/cumem_allocator.cpp` makes the legacy stream depend on the capturing stream. Running it as `hipMemsetAsync` on a private non-blocking stream fixes it.
- vLLM custom allreduce needs the same unregistered capture path as on CUDA (`hipIpcGetMemHandle` fails on cuMem memory). QuickReduce needs no change. RCCL honours `NCCL_GRAPH_REGISTER`, so the existing guard applies.
- With that patch, DeepSeek-V2-Lite TP2 stays bit-exact over 10 cycles plus a level-2 reload, but the graph pool is only 72–244 MiB per GPU: most graph memory (0.95–1.7 GiB) is held by the HIP runtime outside torch pools. Unlike CUDA, ROCm returns it when graphs are destroyed, so destroy-and-recapture would be the better option there (9–50 s per wake).

ROCm support is left for a follow-up.
